claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr contains local microstructural domains with different thermal expansion behavior.
Thermal expansion mismatch between these domains generates internal stresses.
Mismatch-induced internal stresses alter dislocation behavior.
Mismatch-induced coherency stresses govern the unresolved creep, cold-work hardening, and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Conventionally processed HfNbTaTiZr has inherent microchemical inhomogeneities and subtle phase variations.
A homogenization anneal or controlled thermal cycling can reduce thermal expansion mismatch among domains in HfNbTaTiZr.
An intervention-treated sample set will be compared with a conventionally processed control set.
Elasticity and microhardness will be assessed from room temperature to approximately 1100 K, creep near 1250 °C, and aging at 600–800 °C.
Thermal expansion mismatch produces coherent internal stresses at grain boundaries and within grains.
Differences in local thermal expansion coefficients produce residual stresses during cooling from high temperature.
The residual stresses modify dislocation mobility.
The residual stresses influence the stability and behavior of nanoprecipitates or local phase variations.
Changes in dislocation mobility and precipitate or phase behavior alter creep rate, work hardening, and elastic modulus.
Samples treated to reduce thermal expansion mismatch will have lower internal residual stresses than baseline samples.
Reducing thermal expansion mismatch will decrease creep resistance at 1250 °C.
Reducing thermal expansion mismatch will alter microhardness evolution during cold rolling.
Reducing thermal expansion mismatch will shift elastic moduli over 293–1100 K.
Accentuated thermal expansion mismatch will enhance strength and hardening.
The proposed effect will be strongest during rapid cooling, at high testing temperatures, and during aging at 600–800 °C.
Precipitation kinetics and other strengthening mechanisms may confound the effect attributed to thermal expansion mismatch.
